ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Directions are marked on the left side of the figure, with N at the top and S at the bottom; the horizontal line represents the ground, and the flagpoles at a and b are of equal height. The legend shows that black is the shadow length on June 22, and white is hollow and is the shadow length on December 22. At place a, the white shadow on December 22 points north and is relatively long, and the black shadow on June 22 is the shortest, almost very short; at place b, the black shadow on June 22 points south and is relatively long, and the white shadow on December 22 points north and is relatively short, but is still longer than the shortest shadow of place a on June 22. Reasoning: The flagpoles are of equal height and all are at noon; the shorter the shadow length, the greater the solar altitude. The shadow of place a on June 22 is the shortest, indicating that place a is close to the Tropic of Cancer; the shadow of place b on December 22 is relatively short, indicating that place b is located in the low latitudes of the Southern Hemisphere, close to but relatively farther from the Tropic of Capricorn. From the comparison of the shortest shadow lengths in the figure, it can be judged that the absolute value of the latitude of place a is greater than that of place b, that is, |φ_a|>|φ_b|. The geostrophic deflection force increases as the absolute value of latitude increases, so the geostrophic deflection force at place a is greater. Conclusion: place a.
